links.reason: Both verses have the slipping bangle at the shore lord's leaving (இறைஇறவா நின்ற வளை / நல்வளை சோர), a common topos. The venba's கள்ள மனத்தான் is the speaker's own charge, not something the bangle 'convicts' him of, so the teaches sentence reads a qualification into a shared image.

The formal parallel is real: both are send-offs promising jewels (சேயிழை பெறுகுவை / நன்கலம் பெறுகுவை) and both rank the patron above a river image with -இனும் (நீரினும் இனிய சாயல் / நீர்வழிக் கரும்பினும் ... அளி). But teaches rests on Patitruppattu 86, which is not in the packet, and on an unprovable claim that the poet split Kapilar's poem.

The idyll's list echoes Akananuru 122 closely: காவலர் கடுகினும் / காவலர் கடுகுவர், கதநாய் குரைப்பினும / ஞாளி, நீ துயில் எழினும் / அன்னை துஞ்சாள், நிலவு வெளிப்படினும் / மண்டிலம் நின்று விரியும். The difference teaches names is in the Tamil: the girl complains to her friend (பல்முட்டின்றால் நம் களவே), while the idyll tells the mother he goes back without anger (பெயரினும் முனியலுறாஅன்).

The word ஊராண்மை really is shared. But the venba does not claim that ஊராண்மை is swagger. It mocks him for passing off his visit to that street as ஊராண்மை (ஊராண்மை யாக்கிக் கொளல்), which takes the virtue's sense for granted, as teaches itself admits. So there is no tension, only an ironic use of the Kural's word.

The phrase தழங்கு(கு)ரல் முரசம் is shared, but it is a stock camp formula. Akananuru 24 already sets the man's sleepless camp against his wife's lonely night (தமியள் நீந்தி ... யாமே ... பாசறையேமே), so the 'duty and longing at once' that teaches claims for the pair is in one poem alone.

The reversal is real: குறுமகள் அல்லது மருந்து பிறிது இல்லை in Natrinai 80 against வரினும் நோய் மருந்து அல்லர் in Natrinai 64. But these are different speakers about different people, so it is not an incompatible claim about the same thing. As a shared figure turned around it is apt.

The friend's அஞ்சுவது அஞ்சா அறன் இலி அல்லன் (l.26) echoes the Kural's அஞ்சுவ தஞ்சாமை பேதைமை almost word for word, and turns the Kural's folly (பேதைமை) into lawlessness (அறன் இலி) in a lover. That is a real development from prudence to character.
links.text_issue: Lines 11-22 and 25-32, including line 26, are flagged as absent from sangamtamil.com; the link depends on line 26.

links.reason: Paripadal 8.13-16 (நின் ஈன்ற நிரை இதழ்த் தாமரை ... பொய்கையோடு ஒக்கும் நின் குன்றின் ... சுனை) refers back to the birth story of 5.48-49 (இமயத்து நீலப் பைஞ்சுனைப் பயந்தோர் ... பதுமத்துப் பாயல்). Line 11, பரங்குன்று இமயக் குன்றம் நிகர்க்கும், states the transfer of sanctity that teaches describes.

Both verses set the girl's life against his going: வல்வரவு வாழ்வார்க்கு உரை in the Kural and எம்மெல் ஓதி அழிவிலள் எனினே in the poem. One refuses his comfort and the other tempts him with the cool spell (தண்பத வேனில் இன்ப நுகர்ச்சி எம்மொடு கொண்மோ), so the bitter and sweet strategies are real.

The shared terms are real: நல்குவர் / நல்கின், and the gossiping town (கெளவை எடுக்கும் இவ்வூர் / அழுங்கல் ஊர்). But the kuravai in Ainkurunuru 181 belongs to the girls on the sand who describe his shore (குப்பை வெண்மணல் குரவை நிறூஉம் துறை). The poem does not make the town's noise turn into a festive kuravai, so the teaches sentence overreads it.

In the lines given, அடி is the foot of the hill (குன்றத்து அடி உறை இயைக), not the god's feet. The note's line 68 (நின் அடி உறை) is outside the packet's span and cannot be checked. The link turns on the double sense of அடி and sets it against the Kural's escape from rebirth (இறைவன் அடிசேராதார்), and the poem says nothing about rebirth.

Ainkurunuru 281 blesses the parrots for காவல் காட்டியவ்வே, and in Natrinai 134 the parent sends the girl to drive the parrots from the millet on the very hill where the lover set his sign (காதலர் வரு குறி செய்த வரையகச் சிறு தினை ... அவணை ஆக என ஏயள்). The pair does show the field watch set up by agents who do not know what they serve.
links.text_issue: Natrinai 134 line 6 is a strong variant (ஏவினன் மன்னே நுந்தை, யாயும்), which changes who gives the order but not the point.

links.reason: The gesture is shared and distinctive: புதல்வற் றழீஇயினன் ... புறங்கவைஇயினளே in Kuruntokai 359 and சிறுபுறம் கவையினனாக in Akananuru 26, after she turns to the son (மகன் வயின் பெயர்தந்தேனே). The roles are reversed as teaches says, and the child mediates in both.

Both say that evening's pain is known only through his absence: சிறுபுன் மாலை உண்மை அறிவேன் ... அவர்க் காணா ஊங்கே against மாலைநோய் செய்தல் மணந்தார் அகலாத காலை அறிந்ததிலேன். The poem adds the bird leaving its day-tree lonely (பகலுறை முதுமரம் புலம்பப் போகும்), and that is the scene teaches names.

The formula line is shared: விளைந்துகு தீம்பழம். But in Kuruntokai 8 the other woman mocks him as his wife's mirror-puppet (ஆடிப் பாவை போல), not boasting that she caught him. In Ainkurunuru 61 the fruit is description of Kazhar, the measure of the good women (கழாஅர் அன்ன நல்லோர்). Reading the fruit as the man is not fixed by either poem.

Both rank the one who bears abuse (வைதாரின் நல்லர் பொறுப்பவர் / இன்னாச்சொல் நோற்கிற்பவர் ... துறந்தாரின் தூய்மை உடையர்), and the difference in what each compares against is accurate. Still, it is the shared topic of forbearance with a small observation added. Calling the renouncer comparison a 'reward' is loose.

Both use the paalai topos of a male beast caring for its pregnant mate (கடுஞ்சூல் மடப்பிடி தழீஇய / வயவுறு பிணவிற்கு). But Akananuru 197's comfort is that he will not delay (நீடலர்), and nothing says it assumes he will see and remember. Ainkurunuru 323 does not 'confirm' a different poem's comfort, so teaches builds a story from a common motif.

The lizard's cry links them in the same verb: உள்ளுதொறு படூஉம் பல்லி, which the returning man imagines as medicine, and வரக்கண்டு வாய்மாண்ட பல்லி படும, the chirp heard at home as he comes. Together they give the two ends of one omen belief, as teaches says.

Both have bangles slipping (எல்வளை ஞெகிழ / எவ்வளையோ ... உதிர்வன) and bursting bamboo. But in Akananuru 185 the bowstring is only a simile for the sound of bursting (மள்ளர் வில்விசையின் உடைய), not violence on his road. The venba does not say he seeks wealth, so the danger-to-waste contrast is overread from a stock paalai image.
links.text_issue: Thinaimozhi 18 line 3 (எதிர்வன போல்இலவே) is hard to construe.

links.reason: Both suppose that there is no reward beyond: செய்யா உலகத்து நுகர்ச்சி இல்லெனின் and மேலுலகம் இல்லெனினும். The Kural stops at ஈதலே நன்று, while the king falls back on release and fame (மாறிப் பிறப்பின் இன்மையும் கூடும் ... தம்மிசை நட்டு). That is a real difference in how each answers the doubt.

The heart going to the lover is a broad shared motif. Kainnilai 6's உரையா வழங்கும் என் நெஞ்சு says nothing about a gift, or about him being near or far. The contrast teaches draws, between chiding and a secret gift judged by nearness, is imposed on the two verses.

The opening formula is shared word for word (நெருநை ... ஆடினை என்ப ... மகிழ்ந). Akananuru 266 then sets the uproar aside (அவலம் அன்றுமன் எமக்கே) for the oath (சேஎயொடு உற்ற சூளே), while Ainkurunuru 71 ends on the gossip that cannot be hidden. The pair shows exactly the prefix-versus-whole difference teaches claims.

The link is on the memory of his grace: அவன் அளித்த போழ்தே against அளியின்மை ஆற்ற நினைந்து. The contrast of private lament with words to the mother (அன்னை வாழி) holds, but 'public evidence' leans on the decade title, and the pairing is mainly the shared situation of grace remembered after desertion.

சோறுவாய்த்து ஒழிந்தோர் உள்ளியும் puts the patron in the camp thinking of men who repaid his rice with their deaths, and that is the relation புரந்தார் in Kural 780 assumes. The idyll shows him thinking (உள்ளி) rather than weeping, so teaches' 'grief' is slightly generous but grounded.

The Kosar are named in both: வலம்புரி கோசர் அவைக்களத்தானும் and ஊர்முது கோசர் நவைத்த சிறுமையின். The akam poet uses them in the Anni Minili revenge simile, and the note and teaches say so. But Purananuru 283 is broken around that line, so what the puram poem says of the Kosar's council cannot be fixed.
links.text_issue: Purananuru 283 lines 7 and 12 have gaps; line 3 differs in another edition.

links.reason: Both end on the rightward rising cloud as the sure omen (வலனேருங் கார் / வைகலும் ஏரும் வலம், ஐயந்தீர் காட்சி). The Ainthinai verse wraps the cloud in the emblems of Mal, Murugan and Shiva, where Kar Narpathu relies on வைகலும. The contrast teaches draws is in the text.

The madal is the specific institution in both: காமுற்றார் ஏறும் மடல் and மடல் மா ஊர்ந்து ... நாடும் ஊரும் ஒள்நுதல் அரிவை நலம் பாராட்டி. The Natrinai threat spreads the girl's name through towns, so his lost shame (நாண்) would become her exposure, which teaches rightly draws out for the friend who is listening.

The two halves fit closely: the searcher who worships (தொழுவேன், Natrinai 198 l.5) and the onlookers who answer one who folds hands and asks again and again (பரந்துகை தொழுது பல்லூழ் மறுகி வினவுவோயே ... கண்டனெம் மன்ற). Teaches' 'one recognised scene' is supported.

There is a real echo: the sad-eyed evening, புன்கண் அந்தி / புன்கண்ணை ... மாலை. But the Kural asks whether evening's partner is as hard as hers, not where evening reaches, so teaches misdescribes the couplet. Its 'both turn grief into a question about where evening reaches' fits only Natrinai 343 (இல்லைகொல் ... சென்ற நாட்டே).

The idyll shows hospitable dry-land farmers with ploughs (கலப்பை சார்த்தி) feeding the bard varagu and avarai. The Kural praises those who live by the plough (உழுதுண்டு வாழ்வாரே வாழ்வார்), which is consistent with that scene. Reading the Kural as a moral claim against the patronage order is not in either text.

The verbal match is close: தெறூஉம் / தண்ணென்னும் in the Kural against தெறுதலின் வெய்ய / தண்ணிய in Ainkurunuru 322. On a plain reading, distance from her burns in the couplet, while in the poem thought of her while far away cools (உள்ளுதொறும் தண்ணிய வாயின). The note and teaches state the dependence correctly.

The same event and the same patron: Porunar praises Karikalan for the two kings falling at Venni (இருபெரு வேந்தரும் ஒருகளத்து அவிய வெண்ணித் தாக்கிய), while Purananuru 66 tells him to his face that the one who sat facing north from shame at a back wound is better (நின்னினும் நல்லன் அன்றே ... புறப்புண் நாணி வடக்கிருந்தோனே). This is a real tension in how the victory is valued.

Conditional and fulfilment match in wording: வெஞ்சின வேந்தன் வினைவிடப் பெறினே ... தொன்னலம் பெறூஉம் against வேந்துதொழில் விட்டென ... தோள்கவின் எய்தின. Both make her recovery hang on the king's release, as teaches says.

The image is specific and shared: முறை தளர்ந்த மன்னவன் கீழ்க் குடி போலக் ... பனி வாரும் கண் and the afflicted people's tears in Kural 555. But Kalittokai 34 says nothing of tears wearing down the one who caused them, and it frames her as wishing to hide his fault (தீமை மறைப்பென்மன்). The 'threat' that teaches carries over is imported from the Kural.

Both have pallor spreading at the instant of his going: இனிச் சென்றனனே ... திருநுதல் ஊர்தரும் பசப்பே and உவக்காண் ... செல்வார் இவக்காண் ... பசப்பூர்வது. The poem's question to the pallor (யாங்கு அறிந்தன்று) and the chariot scene are the additions teaches names.

Kuruntokai 272 likens her eyes to the bloody arrow her brothers drew from the stag (தன்னையர் ... குருதியொடு பறித்த செங்கோல் வாளி மாறுகொண்டன்ன உண்கண்), beside a doe (மடமான்). There is a link to the Kural's Death-eye-doe. But the doe in the poem is not her look, so 'staging the three-way question' needs a generous reading. The kin-threat point is grounded in தன்னையர்.

The parallel is close: the embrace weighed against both worlds (உலகமும் புத்தேள் நாடும் இரண்டும் தூக்கிற் சீர்சாலாவே) and against Vishnu's world (தாமரைக் கண்ணான் உலகு). But teaches claims that the Kural alludes to the Sangam verdict, which neither text shows.

The half-line is near-identical: ஏறோடு ... மணி நாகம் அனுங்க in both, in the returning man's mouth (Kar Narpathu 20) and in the friend's prediction (Thinaimozhi 28). Teaches' modest claim, that this is a shared formula of the mullai rains, is what the pair shows.

Natrinai 52 does not deny that effort brings wealth. It calls the heart set on ஆள்வினை loveless (அன்பு இலை) and the wealth slight beside the embrace (ஐது ஏகு அம்ம இயைந்து செய் பொருளே). That limits the Kural's முயற்சி திருவினை ஆக்கும and does not contradict it, so 'incompatible claims' overstates.

Both have the premise: மன்னாப் பொருள் and அற்கா இயல்பிற்று செல்வம். But in Natrinai 71 it is a single epithet in the first line. The friend's case rests on the leave-taking and the moaning dove (வீழ் துணைப் பயிரும் கையறு முரல் குரல்), not on impermanence. The 'before it was a doctrine' chronology is unsupported.

The son works on both sides: in Akananuru 66 he draws the father home (மகனொடு தானே புகுதந்தோனே), and in the venba the wife names him her companion to dismiss the bard (சிறுவன் உடையேன் துணை ... எழுந்தீக). Teaches' 'way in and reason to keep him out' is accurate to both.

On the surface there is a real tension in the shared root இர-: இரந்துகோள் தக்கது in 780 against இரவின் இளிவந்தது இல் in 1066, where even begging water for a cow is the worst disgrace. Teaches states the resolution, that 780 uses the worst disgrace as its measure, and this is true and specific.

Both place the hill by Koodal: கூடற் குடவயின் ... குன்றமர்ந்து உறைதலும் and குன்றத்தான் கூடல் வரவு. That tie is the real connection. The bees and blooming pools are stock, and the procession reading of கூடல் வரவு is one construal.
links.text_issue: Paripadal 8 lines 23-24 (the bees and pools) are flagged as absent from sangamtamil.com.

iraicchi.act: carries the paddy ear off into its own cool mud hole
iraicchi.sense: the town's man takes his pleasure off to a place of his own while she wastes away

poems.note: The crab can be read as a scene mapped part by part, but the infidelity it points to is not stated in the poem or its thurai, so only the single-carrier reading holds.

iraicchi.act: cries again and again for the mate it cannot find
iraicchi.sense: if he leaves, his beloved will call for him like the bereft female bird

poems.note: The elephant is an openly decoded figure for a woman (வன முலை, வெண் பல் நகை), not a hidden comparison.
The colophon's thinai is வாகை (puram), so both fields are null although the dove pair in lines 45-48 would otherwise be a candidate.

iraicchi.act: lays its eggs safe inside the boat's hull
iraicchi.sense: as the little crow makes its home and young in the shore boat, the shore lord should take her into his home

poems.note: The dove that escaped the hunter's net and now fears a spider's thread acts like a person, but what it implies for the lovers cannot be said in one sure sentence.
Lines 5-7 (the empty commons and the post) are hard to construe.

iraicchi.act: comes home at dusk and rests with its young under the eaves
iraicchi.sense: even the house sparrow is with its family at evening, while he stays away

iraicchi.act: draws water with its trunk and runs to give it to its mate
iraicchi.sense: even the tusker on his road serves its mate, so the man who went that way will remember and return
